title: Orenburg-inspired cobweb shawl
subtitle: A lace-weight square cobweb shawl inspired by the Russian Orenburg tradition.
excerpt: A square cobweb shawl in lace-weight yarn inspired by the Russian Orenburg tradition: a fine mesh body with small geometric motifs at the corners, worked centre-out. Finished size approximately 110 × 110 cm when blocked. About 150 g of 2-ply lace-weight yarn. This is one of the most demanding shawls in the collection.
sourceNotes: The Orenburg shawl tradition is documented in Carol R. Noble, The Art of Orenburg Lace Knitting (2006) and in Galina Khmeleva and Carol R. Noble, Gossamer Webs (1998). The mesh pattern (patterned net stitch) and geometric corner motifs are traditional Russian public domain forms predating any specific modern publication. This pattern is an original synthesis inspired by the tradition, not a direct reproduction of any specific chart.

glossaryTerms.definition: The characteristic background stitch of Russian Orenburg shawls: a fine allover net pattern of yarn-overs and decreases creating a regular grid of small square holes. Also called patterned net or Russian mesh.
A length of smooth waste yarn threaded through all live stitches at a given row, allowing safe rip-back.

content.text: A centre-out square cobweb shawl in lace-weight yarn, worked in fine
Orenburg mesh
with geometric corner motifs. Finished size approximately 110 × 110 cm.
This is one of the most technically demanding shawls in the collection. Approximately 320 RS rows total at 2.75 mm and lace weight. Thread a
lifeline

every 50 rows without fail. Budget about 150 g (about 1,500 m / 1,640 yards) of 2-ply lace-weight yarn. Traditional Orenburg uses a blend of fine goat down and silk; a fine merino lace yarn works well.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 150 g (1,500 m / 1,640 yards) of 2-ply lace-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 2.75 mm (UK 12 / US 2) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4 corner markers, several more for repeat boundaries

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

32 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over Orenburg mesh on 2.75 mm needles, blocked. At gauge a 110 × 110 cm square requires approximately 352 stitches per side (32 sts × 11 = 352) and approximately 484 rows total (44 rows × 11 = 484). At 8 stitches gained per RS row from the centre-out construction, 352 RS rows bring the shawl to full size.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on and centre growth

Cast on 8 stitches. Place 4 corner markers (after sts 2, 4, 6). Work the standard centre-out square RS increase row: *k to marker, yo, SM, yo; repeat from * 3 more times, k to end. WS rows: p all sts. Work in plain stockinette until each quarter holds at least 20 stitches, then introduce Orenburg mesh.
Orenburg mesh body

Once the sections are large enough, replace the plain stockinette body with Orenburg mesh. RS row: *k to marker, yo, SM, yo, then work mesh row across body sts; repeat from * for all 4 quarters. Mesh RS row (2 sts): yo, k2tog. Mesh WS row: p all sts. The mesh creates a regular grid of small square holes. Continue to full size.
Corner motifs

In the final 20 RS rows, substitute a simple 8-stitch geometric diamond motif around each corner marker: k3, yo, ssk, k1, k2tog, yo, k3. Work this motif centred on each corner in the last 20 rows before bind-off while maintaining the mesh body in the remaining stitches.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off. The full bind-off row holds approximately 2,816 stitches at gauge.
Common faults
Mesh holes closing up on WS rows: the WS purl row was worked too tight. Work WS rows loosely; at 2-ply lace weight a tight purl closes the mesh holes before blocking.

Corner increase yo lost in the mesh: the two corner yo increases sit at the markers; the mesh yo occurs 1 to 2 stitches away. Mark the corner increases with a different coloured marker to distinguish them from mesh yarn-overs.
Blocking

Soak 30 minutes in cool water. Use a very large blocking surface: a 110 × 110 cm square needs at least a 120 × 120 cm flat surface. Pin all four corners first. Pin along all four edges using close pins spaced no more than 5 cm apart. The mesh opens dramatically: the pre-blocking shawl will be about 60 × 60 cm and expands to 110 × 110 cm under pinning. Leave 36 to 48 hours.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water. Lay flat to dry. Re-block after every few wears as the mesh contracts.
What to try next

The full Orenburg tradition adds a separate knitted border along all four edges, picked up and worked after the main body is complete. The border uses the same mesh with a zigzag outer edge, adding 5 to 8 cm to each side.
